title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking
source_locator: Fig. 2h-j; Extended Data Fig. 3; Methods 'Optogenetics experiments with 3D joint kinematics'; Supplementary Video 1
quote: DNg100 activation produced forward walking on the ball, but at a lower speed than is typical of wild-type flies [53].
mapping_basis: Paper uses the MANC type name DNg100 (and notes it is BDN2 in Sapkal et al. 2024); the split VT058557-AD x R85F12-DBD is listed in driver_lines.csv as DNg100.
stimulation: 638 nm laser, 1200 Hz, 30% duty cycle, focused at front left body-coxa joint; 5 s on; 0.03, 0.09 and 0.33 mW/mm2 (strongest 0.33 mW/mm2)
sensory_condition: decapitated, de-winged, tethered on air-supported spherical treadmill
frequency_note: L1 step frequency read from Fig. 2j: medians roughly 3.5, 5.1 and 5.5 Hz at 0.03, 0.09 and 0.33 mW/mm2; frequency increased with laser intensity
coordination_notes: generally tetrapod coordination (Methods; Extended Data Fig. 3)
n_flies_note: n=7 flies, 8 trials per fly per intensity
notes: Walking initiated in headless flies; forward velocity and stepping frequency increased with laser intensity (Fig. 2i-j). Walking coded yes for all three leg pairs per PROTOCOL 3. Driver line written as given in the genotype table (page 29); driver_lines.csv lists the same hemidriver pair as 'BDN2-splitGal4' / 'VT058557-p65ADZp(attP40);R85F12-ZpGDBD(attP2)'. Simulation rhythmicity scores for DNg100 seen in Fig. 1e/Fig. 2 (not used as evidence).

title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking
source_locator: Fig. 5c-e; Results 'A separate class of descending neurons recruits an overlapping rhythm generating circuit'; Supplementary Video 2
quote: we optogenetically activated DNb08 neurons in decapitated flies and found that they reliably produced rhythmic leg movements
mapping_basis: Paper uses the MANC type name DNb08; SS70620 is listed in driver_lines.csv as DNb08.
stimulation: 638 nm laser, 1200 Hz, 30% duty cycle, focused at front left body-coxa joint; 5 s on (intensity for DNb08 not stated)
sensory_condition: decapitated, de-winged, tethered; legs unloaded (spherical treadmill removed, per Fig. 5d schematic and text)
coordination_notes: Movements resembled searching movements of legs not in contact with the ground, qualitatively different from coordinated walking; only left front and left middle femur-tibia joints quantified
penetrance: front and middle leg kinematic rhythmicity significantly higher stim-on vs stim-off (p = 0.036, 0.004)
n_flies_note: n=10 flies, 8 stim-on and 4 stim-off trials per fly
notes: Fig. 5d traces show many femur-tibia cycles in front and middle legs during stimulation; Fig. 5e quantifies a kinematic rhythmicity score (applied to real joint-angle traces). Hind legs not reported. Surface coded air because Fig. 5d schematic shows no ball and the text says movements were more reliable with the treadmill removed; the paper does not say explicitly which surface the Fig. 5e data came from. On-ball condition recorded separately (a5-g05-A-0003). Simulation scores for DNb08 seen (Fig. 1e, Fig. 5a-b); not used as evidence.

title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking
source_locator: Results 'A separate class of descending neurons recruits an overlapping rhythm generating circuit'; Discussion 'Limitations'
quote: Indeed, movements were evoked more reliably when the spherical treadmill was removed.
mapping_basis: Paper uses the MANC type name DNb08; SS70620 is listed in driver_lines.csv as DNb08.
stimulation: 638 nm laser, 1200 Hz, 30% duty cycle; 5 s on (intensity not stated)
sensory_condition: decapitated, tethered on spherical treadmill (legs loaded)
penetrance: less reliable than with treadmill removed (not quantified)
notes: On-ball condition is only mentioned qualitatively: the movements were evoked less reliably on the treadmill than with it removed ('DNb08-driven movements were more consistent when fly's legs were unloaded'). Which legs moved, and whether they moved rhythmically, on the ball is not reported, so all pairs are unclear.
